# Load initial data
This is a table with a row for each game per team. So two rows per game, one for the home and away team.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
Team_Data <- read_csv("data/TeamStatistics.csv")
```

# Filter data to certain date
Also we only want the rows from the perspective of away teams.

```{r}
Team_Data <- Team_Data %>%
  filter(year(gameDate)>=2015,home == 0)
```


# disambiguate city names
Lakers and Clipper both play in LA
```{r}

travelingCities <- Team_Data %>%
  pull(teamCity)
travelingNames <- Team_Data %>% 
  pull(teamName)
oppCities <- Team_Data %>%
  pull(opponentTeamCity)
oppNames <- Team_Data %>% 
  pull(opponentTeamName)

cleanCities <- function(cities, names){
  for(i in 1:length(cities)){
    city <- cities[i]
    if(city %in% c("LA", "Los Angeles")){
      if(names[i] == "Lakers"){
        city <- "LA_LAK"
      }else if(names[i] == "Clippers"){
        city <- "LA_CLI"
      }
    }
    cities[i] = city
  }
  return (cities)
}

Team_Data$teamCity <- cleanCities(travelingCities, travelingNames)
Team_Data$opponentTeamCity <- cleanCities(oppCities, oppNames)

rm(travelingCities, travelingNames, oppCities, oppNames, cleanCities)

```

# generate distances
Using the Lookup table to add a column travelDist, which is the estimated travel distance, calculated as the distance between the home team and the away team.

The details of generating the dist Lookup are abstracted in this report because we believe that that solving that problem was a math question, not a data science one. However, details can be found in the genLocations.R file. For our purposes, assume that distLookup[city1, city2] is the distance between the two cities.
```{r}
readLookup <- read.csv("./generatedData/distLookup.csv", row.names = 1)

travelDists <- 1:nrow(Team_Data)
travelingCities <- Team_Data %>% pull(teamCity)
oppCities <- Team_Data %>% pull(opponentTeamCity)

travelingCities <- gsub(" ", "_", travelingCities)
oppCities <- gsub(" ", "_", oppCities)

for(i in 1:length(travelDists)){
  dist <- readLookup[travelingCities[i],oppCities[i]]
  if(!is.numeric(dist)){
    #print(playerCity)
    #print(oppCity)
    dist <- 0
  }
  travelDists[i] <- dist
}

readLookup[travelingCities[1],oppCities[1]]

Team_Data$travelDist <- travelDists


Team_Data %>% 
  relocate(teamCity, opponentTeamCity, travelDist, .before=1)

Team_Data <- Team_Data %>% 
  relocate(teamCity, opponentTeamCity, travelDist, .before=1) %>% 
  filter(travelDist != 0)
```

# graphing and testing win rate over travel dist
There seems to be no correlation.
See conclusion for more details as to why on we believe we arrived at this surprising conclusion

```{r}
Team_Data <- Team_Data
Team_Data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = travelDist, 
             fill = if_else(win==1, "win", "loss"),
            )
         ) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 100, position = "fill") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("loss" = "#F44336", "win" = "#4CAF50")) +
  labs(
    x = "distance between home and away team (miles)",
    y = "win rate of away teams",
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )

cor.test(Team_Data$travelDist, Team_Data$win)
```
